name: Issue Zero
tagline: Plan, write and grow a newsletter people open
about: Issue Zero is an independent newsletter writer's desk: it drafts issues from raw notes, plans an editorial calendar you can keep, turns reader replies into a mailbag section, plans list growth and reads your issue stats.
persona: You are a newsletter editor who has grown several lists: subject lines that keep promises, issues with one job each, growth without buying attention.

onboarding.title: Send something worth opening
onboarding.subtitle: Your platform and list size shape every suggestion.
bullets: An editorial calendar you can keep
Growth plans sized to your list

profile.label: Newsletter & topic
profile.placeholder: weekly notes on indie game design

tools.title: Draft this issue
tools.subtitle: Notes → a full issue

inputs.label: Raw notes / links / ideas
inputs.placeholder: Three links, one rant about menus, reader question from Priya…

tools.prompt: Draft a {format} issue of the profile newsletter from: {notes}, giving the issue one job. Produce a kv (subject line, preview text, the issue's one job, estimated read time), text with the issue body in the profile platform's conventions with short headed sections, a one-line intro that skips the throat-clearing and a P.S. that asks for a reply, and bullets of 3 alternate subject lines each with its angle (curiosity / benefit / number / personal).

tools.title: Editorial calendar
tools.subtitle: The next 8 issues, planned

inputs.label: Ideas, half-drafts and reader requests
inputs.placeholder: difficulty curves; interview with Mara; the tutorial nobody finished…

tools.prompt: Plan the next 8 issues of the profile newsletter at its cadence starting {start}, from: {ideas}. Produce a table (Issue # | Send date | Working title | Format (essay / links / Q&A / interview) | One job | Material still needed) with exactly 8 rows alternating heavy and light issues, bullets of 3 seasonal or news hooks worth timing an issue to, a callout on which ideas are two issues in disguise or not an issue at all, and a checklist of what to prepare this week for issue #1.

tools.title: Reader mailbag
tools.subtitle: Replies → a Q&A section

inputs.label: Reader replies (paste them)
inputs.placeholder: From Priya: how do you decide when a level is too hard?…

tools.prompt: Build a {length} mailbag section for the profile newsletter from these reader replies: {replies}. Produce cards (one per reply used, meta = reader first name or 'anonymous' · topic) each with the reader's question trimmed to two lines and a 60–100 word answer in the newsletter's voice, bullets on which replies deserve a whole future issue and which to answer privately, a quote with the closing line that invites next issue's replies, and a callout on getting permission before quoting a reader by name.

tools.title: Growth plan
tools.subtitle: From this list size to the next
tools.prompt: Plan growth from the profile's current subscribers to {goal} in {weeks} weeks. Produce a table (Week | Tactic | Effort (hours) | Expected new subs), bullets of 5 tactics that fit the profile platform (recommendations, cross-posts, lead magnet, referrals, repurposing), and a callout on what not to do (bought lists, giveaways that attract the wrong readers).

tools.title: Issue retro
tools.subtitle: Stats → what to change
tools.prompt: Analyse the stats {stats} for an issue that was: {what}, at the profile's list size and cadence. Produce a kv (open-rate verdict, click verdict, reply signal, unsubscribe read), bullets on likely causes, and steps for 3 experiments for the next issue, each with the metric that decides it.
